key_insight: Aletheia, powered by Gemini 3 Deep Think, autonomously solved 6 out of 10 problems in the inaugural FirstProof challenge within the allowed timeframe, demonstrating measurable autonomous progress on formal mathematical tasks.
problem_solved: Can an autonomous AI research agent reliably produce expert-acceptable proofs in a competitive formal-math benchmark (FirstProof) and be evaluated transparently?
method: Run Aletheia (an autonomous agent driven by Gemini 3 Deep Think) on the full FirstProof problem set under the challenge time limits.
Automatically generate candidate proofs and submit results for expert assessment, using majority expert judgments to determine solved problems (experts were not unanimous on Problem 8).
Provide full transparency: explicitly state interpretation of the benchmark and disclose experimental details and protocols.
impact: Demonstrates that large-model–based research agents can autonomously achieve expert-acknowledged results on nontrivial mathematical problems, informing future design and evaluation of AI research assistants and formal-reasoning benchmarks.
visual_elements: Bar chart: problems 1–10 with solved vs. unsolved marking (highlight Problem 8 as contested).
Timeline: challenge time window showing when autonomous runs occurred and solutions produced.
Flow diagram: Aletheia agent -> Gemini 3 Deep Think reasoning -> candidate proofs -> expert assessment.
Icon set: autonomy (robot/agent), mathematics (formal symbol/logic), evaluation (judge/expert), transparency (open document)
paper_authors: Tony Feng, Junehyuk Jung, Sang-hyun Kim, Carlo Pagano, Sergei Gukov
